question: People watched one car-crash film. Asked how fast the cars smashed, or contacted, each other, how far apart were their average estimates?
answer: About 15 km/h. In Loftus and Palmer's 1974 study, smashed drew an average of 40.8 mph and contacted 31.8 mph, a gap of 9 mph. A week later, the smashed group was also likelier to recall broken glass that the film never showed. One verb set the speed before memory did.
move: The words of a question can write the answer before anyone gives it.
ask: When I describe a quarrel to a friend, which of my words already decides who was at fault?
trap: Under 2 km/h, since everyone watched the identical film.
source: Loftus & Palmer, Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior, 1974
reference: Loftus & Palmer, Reconstruction of automobile destruction: an example of the interaction between language and memory, Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior 13(5), 1974
